en.title: Pixar's 'Gatto' Trailer Drops: Is Venice Ready for Mafia Kitties?
en.summary: Pixar's latest teaser for 'Gatto' hints at a charming, visually distinct adventure starring Mark Ruffalo as a Venetian cat. The film aims to recapture the studio's magic with a fresh aesthetic and a story about purpose.
en.body:
After a string of box office disappointments and public relations stumbles, Pixar is banking on a charming ensemble of felines to help restore its legendary reputation. The first teaser for **Enrico Casarosa**'s upcoming film, **Gatto**, has arrived, and it’s asking a question as old as time itself: Do we still love cats? More specifically, do we love *animated* cats navigating the canals of Venice with a hint of mobster swagger?

The trailer offers a glimpse into a world that feels both familiar and refreshingly new for the animation giant. Gone are the hyper-realistic 3D visuals we've come to expect. Instead, **Gatto** embraces a hybridized 2D aesthetic that immediately sets it apart, promising a visual feast that complements its story. At its heart is **Nero**, voiced by **Mark Ruffalo**, a black cat who seems to be grappling with his life choices. The official synopsis teases a narrative where Nero finds himself indebted to a feline mob boss, adding a layer of intrigue to what could otherwise be a simple tale of a cat exploring his city.

This stylistic shift is significant. **Casarosa**, who previously directed the beloved **Luca**, appears to be pushing Pixar's boundaries. While the premise might lean into the sheer joy of watching animated cats be goofy – a concept that, as the trailer suggests, the studio is betting will resonate – the underlying themes of friendship and finding one's purpose, as hinted by web research, could give **Gatto** the emotional depth fans expect.

## A New Look for Pixar

The visual direction of **Gatto** is perhaps its most immediate talking point. By opting for a more stylized, almost painterly 2D look, Pixar is taking a bold step away from its signature 3D rendering. This choice could be a strategic move to differentiate the film in a crowded market and to appeal to viewers seeking something visually distinct. It’s a gamble, but one that could pay off handsomely if it captures the whimsical spirit of Venice while allowing the characters to shine through expressive animation.

> "Indebted to a feline mob boss, a black cat named Nero finds"

This line from the official teaser hints at a narrative that might blend lighthearted animal antics with a more complex, perhaps even comedic, crime-adjacent storyline. It’s a narrative hook that promises more than just cute cats; it suggests a story with stakes, character development, and potentially, some truly memorable moments driven by the voice cast, which also includes **Laurence Fishburne**.

## The Stakes for Pixar

Pixar needs **Gatto** to be more than just a modest success; it needs a win that reaffirms its status as a premier storyteller in animation. The studio has leaned heavily on sequels and pre-existing franchises, with **Toy Story 5** on the horizon, a move that acknowledges the challenges of launching original IP. **Gatto** represents an opportunity to prove that their capacity for original, compelling stories is still very much alive. The success of **Gatto** could be a crucial indicator of Pixar's creative direction for years to come, signaling a willingness to experiment with both visual style and narrative themes.

## What's Next

**Gatto** is slated for release on March 5, 2027. Fans eager to see this new visual style and hear **Mark Ruffalo** bring Nero to life will be watching closely for future trailers and details that flesh out this intriguing Venetian feline adventure.

es.title: Pixar revela el primer tráiler de 'Gatto': ¿Venecia está lista para gatos mafiosos?
es.summary: El estudio de animación Pixar lanza su último teaser para 'Gatto', una aventura visualmente distinta protagonizada por Mark Ruffalo como un gato veneciano. La película busca recuperar su magia con un estilo fresco y una historia sobre propósito.
es.body:
Después de una serie de decepciones en taquilla y problemas de relaciones públicas, Pixar está apostando por un encantador grupo de gatos para ayudar a restaurar su reputación legendaria. El primer teaser para la película de **Enrico Casarosa**, **Gatto**, ha llegado, y plantea una pregunta tan antigua como el tiempo mismo: ¿Aún amamos a los gatos? Más específicamente, ¿Aún amamos a los *gatos animados* que navegan por los canales de Venecia con un toque de orgullo mafioso?

El tráiler ofrece una visión de un mundo que se siente a la vez familiar y frescamente nuevo para el gigante de la animación. Se han ido los visuales en alta definición hiperrrealistas que hemos venido esperando. En su lugar, **Gatto** abraza un estilo híbrido de 2D que lo distingue inmediatamente, prometiendo una fiesta visual que complementa su historia. En su corazón está **Nero**, voz de **Mark Ruffalo**, un gato negro que parece estar luchando con sus decisiones de vida. El resumen oficial sugiere una narrativa donde Nero se encuentra en deuda con un jefe mafioso gato, agregando una capa de intriga a lo que podría ser de lo contrario una historia simple de un gato explorando su ciudad.

Este cambio estilístico es significativo. **Casarosa**, quien anteriormente dirigió el querido **Luca**, parece estar empujando los límites de Pixar. Si bien el argumento podría inclinarse hacia el simple placer de ver a gatos animados ser divertidos — un concepto que, tal como sugiere el tráiler, el estudio está apostando que resonará — los temas subyacentes de amistad y encontrar uno mismo, como se sugiere mediante la investigación en línea, podrían dar a **Gatto** la profundidad emocional que los fans esperan.

## Un Nuevo Apariencia para Pixar

La dirección visual de **Gatto** es quizás su punto de discusión más inmediato. Al optar por un estilo más estilizado, casi pintoresco en 2D, Pixar está tomando un paso audaz hacia su firma. Este cambio podría ser una estrategia para diferenciar la película en un mercado abarrotado y atraer a los espectadores que buscan algo visualmente distinto. Es un riesgo, pero uno que podría pagar ricos si captura el espíritu juguetón de Venecia y permite que los personajes se destaquen a través de animación expresiva.

> "Deudor a un jefe mafioso gato, un gato negro llamado Nero encuentra"

Esta línea del teaser oficial sugiere una narrativa que podría combinar animadas gatos juguetones con una historia más compleja, quizás incluso cómica, relacionada con la delincuencia. Es una trampa narrativa que promete más que solo gatos adorables; sugiere una historia con estakes, desarrollo de personajes y posiblemente, algunos momentos verdaderamente memorables impulsados por el reparto de voces, que también incluye a **Laurence Fishburne**.

## Las Apuestas para Pixar

Pixar necesita que **Gatto** sea más que solo un éxito moderado; necesita una victoria que reafirme su estatus como una de las principales narradoras en animación. El estudio ha apoyado con fuerza secuelas y franquicias existentes, con **Toy Story 5** en el horizonte, una decisión que reconoce los desafíos de lanzar IP original. **Gatto** representa una oportunidad para demostrar que su capacidad para contar historias originales y emocionantes sigue viva. El éxito de **Gatto** podría ser un indicador crucial de la dirección creativa de Pixar por años venideros, señalando una voluntad de experimentar con estilo visual y temas narrativos.

## Próximos Pasos

**Gatto** está programado para estrenarse el 5 de marzo de 2027. Los fanáticos ansiosos por ver este nuevo estilo visual y escuchar a **Mark Ruffalo** dar vida a Nero estarán observando de cerca futuros tráilers y detalles que completen esta aventura feline veneciana intrigante.

content_raw: The last few years have not been great for the former hitmakers over at Pixar, as a series of low-performing films at the box office have collided in the public consciousness with a bunch of frankly terrible PR, as the studio pissed off fans and employees alike by doing things like excising a storyline about a trans kid from its Disney+ TV show Win Or Lose . And while the studio had a mild bounce back earlier this year with February’s Hoppers —which earned both modestly warm reviews and a decent take in theaters with its smaller scale approach—Pixar still needs some serious wins to help reforge its aura of animated invincibility. To face that challenge, the studio has raised a serious question: Y’all still like cats, right? Which is, in fact the major takeaway from the teaser trailer for Pixar’s new film Gatto , which lightly feints toward a more complex “Mafia kitties” conceit before going all-in on just watching animated felines be goofballs. Besides featuring the voices of Laurence Fishburne and Mark Ruffalo as two of the notable toe-bean possessors, the trailer does  offer a good look at the movie’s animation style, which forgoes the studio’s more traditional 3D visuals in favor of a hybridized two-dimensional look that sets itself apart from Pixar’s usual output. This latest Pixar offering arrives courtesy of director Enrico Casarosa, who previously helmed 2021’s Luca , and apparently centers on Ruffalo’s Nero, a black cat living in Venice. Pixar is, of course, currently gearing up for the release of its next film,  Toy Story 5 , which will likely be a pretty major hit. (The studio has struggled a lot more with original IP in recent years than its tried-and-true franchises, and hasn’t been shy about throwing the full weight of the Disney release machine behind this latest installment.) Gatto  won’t be out in theaters until 2027, when it’ll slink its way into theaters in March.
